requirements.original: decvalue(inout bitstring encoded_value, out any decoded_value, in universal charstring decoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return integer
requirements.canonical: The `decvalue` predefined function has the signature decvalue(inout bitstring encoded_value, out any decoded_value, in universal charstring decoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return integer.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.2 -- decvalue(inout bitstring encoded_value, out any decoded_value, in universal charstring decoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return integer

requirements.original: The decvalue function decodes a bitstring into a value.
requirements.canonical: The `decvalue` function IS the predefined function that decodes a bitstring into a value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.2 -- The decvalue function decodes a bitstring into a value.

requirements.original: The optional dynamic_encoding parameter is used for dynamic selection of encode attribute of the decoded_value parameter for this single decvalue call.
requirements.canonical: The optional `dynamic_encoding` parameter of `decvalue` IS used for dynamic selection of the encode attribute of the `decoded_value` parameter for this single `decvalue` call.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.2 -- The optional dynamic_encoding parameter is used for dynamic selection of encode attribute of the decoded_value parameter for this single decvalue call.

requirements.original: The rules for dynamic selection of the encode attribute are described in clause 27.9.
requirements.canonical: The dynamic selection of the encode attribute in a call of `decvalue` IS governed by the rules of clause 27.9.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.2 -- The rules for dynamic selection of the encode attribute are described in clause 27.9.

requirements.original: If the decoding was successful, then the used bits are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue` is successful, the part of `encoded_value` consumed by decoding (the used bits) IS removed from the `encoded_value` parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.2 -- If the decoding was successful, then the used bits are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.

requirements.original: If the decoding was successful, then the used bits are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue` is successful, the remaining undecoded part of the input IS returned in the `encoded_value` parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.2 -- If the decoding was successful, then the used bits are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.

requirements.original: If the decoding was successful, then the used bits are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue` is successful, the decoded value IS returned in the `decoded_value` parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.2 -- If the decoding was successful, then the used bits are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.

requirements.original: If the decoding was unsuccessful, the actual parameters for encoded_value and decoded_value are not changed.
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue` is unsuccessful, the value of each of the actual parameters for `encoded_value` and `decoded_value` IS NOT changed.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.2 -- If the decoding was unsuccessful, the actual parameters for encoded_value and decoded_value are not changed.

requirements.original: The function shall return an integer value to indicate success or failure of the decoding below:
requirements.canonical: The `decvalue` function SHALL return an integer value indicating success or failure of the decoding.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.2 -- The function shall return an integer value to indicate success or failure of the decoding below:

requirements.original: The return value 0 indicates that decoding was successful.
requirements.canonical: The return value 0 of `decvalue` IS the indication that decoding was successful.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.2 -- The return value 0 indicates that decoding was successful.

requirements.original: The return value 1 indicates an unspecified cause of decoding failure.
requirements.canonical: The return value 1 of `decvalue` IS the indication of an unspecified cause of decoding failure.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.2 -- The return value 1 indicates an unspecified cause of decoding failure.

requirements.original: This value is also returned if the encoded_value parameter contains an unitialized value.
requirements.canonical: If the `encoded_value` actual parameter of `decvalue` contains an uninitialized value, `decvalue` SHALL return 1.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.2 -- This value is also returned if the encoded_value parameter contains an unitialized value.

requirements.original: The return value 2 indicates that decoding could not be completed as encoded_value did not contain enough bits.
requirements.canonical: The return value 2 of `decvalue` IS the indication that decoding could not be completed because `encoded_value` did not contain enough bits.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.2 -- The return value 2 indicates that decoding could not be completed as encoded_value did not contain enough bits.

requirements.original: The restrictions in clause 16.1.2 apply.
requirements.canonical: Each restriction of clause 16.1.2 IS applicable to `decvalue`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.2 -- The restrictions in clause 16.1.2 apply.

requirements.original: encvalue_unichar(in template (value) any inpar, in charstring string_serialization := "UTF-8", in universal charstring encoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return universal charstring
requirements.canonical: The `encvalue_unichar` predefined function has the signature encvalue_unichar(in template (value) any inpar, in charstring string_serialization := "UTF-8", in universal charstring encoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return universal charstring.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.3 -- encvalue_unichar(in template (value) any inpar, in charstring string_serialization := "UTF-8", in universal charstring encoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return universal charstring

requirements.original: The encvalue_unichar function encodes a value or template into a universal charstring.
requirements.canonical: The `encvalue_unichar` function IS the predefined function that encodes a value or template into a universal charstring.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.3 -- The encvalue_unichar function encodes a value or template into a universal charstring.

requirements.original: When the actual parameter that is passed to inpar is a template, it shall resolve to a specific value (the same restrictions apply as for the argument of the send statement).
requirements.canonical: When the actual parameter passed to the `inpar` formal parameter of `encvalue_unichar` is a template, the template SHALL resolve to a specific value.
requirements.condition: the actual parameter passed to inpar is a template

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.3 -- When the actual parameter that is passed to inpar is a template, it shall resolve to a specific value (the same restrictions apply as for the argument of the send statement).

requirements.original: The returned universal charstring represents the encoded value of inpar, however, the TTCN-3 test system need not make any check on its correctness.
requirements.canonical: The universal charstring returned by `encvalue_unichar` IS the encoded value of `inpar`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.3 -- The returned universal charstring represents the encoded value of inpar, however, the TTCN-3 test system need not make any check on its correctness.

requirements.original: If the optional string_serialization parameter is omitted, the default value "UTF-8" is used.
requirements.canonical: If the optional `string_serialization` parameter of `encvalue_unichar` is omitted, the default value "UTF-8" IS used.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.3 -- If the optional string_serialization parameter is omitted, the default value "UTF-8" is used.

requirements.original: The optional dynamic_encoding parameter is used for dynamic selection of encode attribute of the inpar value for this single encvalue_unichar call.
requirements.canonical: The optional `dynamic_encoding` parameter of `encvalue_unichar` IS used for dynamic selection of the encode attribute of the `inpar` value for this single `encvalue_unichar` call.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.3 -- The optional dynamic_encoding parameter is used for dynamic selection of encode attribute of the inpar value for this single encvalue_unichar call.

requirements.original: The rules for dynamic selection of the encode attribute are described in clause 27.9.
requirements.canonical: The dynamic selection of the encode attribute in a call of `encvalue_unichar` IS governed by the rules of clause 27.9.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.3 -- The rules for dynamic selection of the encode attribute are described in clause 27.9.

requirements.original: The following values (see ISO/IEC 10646 [2]) are allowed as string_serialization actual parameters (for the description of the UCS encoding scheme see clause 27.5): a) "UTF-8" b) "UTF-16" c) "UTF-16LE" d) "UTF-16BE" e) "UTF-32" f) "UTF-32LE" g) "UTF-32BE"
requirements.canonical: The `string_serialization` actual parameter of `encvalue_unichar` SHALL be one of "UTF-8", "UTF-16", "UTF-16LE", "UTF-16BE", "UTF-32", "UTF-32LE" or "UTF-32BE".
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.3 -- The following values (see ISO/IEC 10646 [2]) are allowed as string_serialization actual parameters (for the description of the UCS encoding scheme see clause 27.5): a) "UTF-8" b) "UTF-16" c) "UTF-16LE" d) "UTF-16BE" e) "UTF-32" f) "UTF-32LE" g) "UTF-32BE"

requirements.original: The serialized bitstring shall not include the optional signature (see clause 10 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2], also known as byte order mark).
requirements.canonical: The octet serialization of the characters used by `encvalue_unichar` SHALL NOT include the optional signature (byte order mark).

readings: The octet serialization of the characters used by `encvalue_unichar` SHALL NOT include the optional signature (byte order mark).
The `encvalue_unichar` function SHALL NOT produce or expect a byte order mark in the bitstring exchanged with the codec.
The universal charstring handled by `encvalue_unichar` SHALL NOT start with the character U+FEFF.
ambiguity.issue: 'The serialized bitstring' is not a parameter or result of `encvalue_unichar` (which handles a universal charstring); it is unclear which bit/octet sequence must be free of the BOM. The first reading (the intermediate octet serialization) was chosen.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.3 -- The serialized bitstring shall not include the optional signature (see clause 10 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2], also known as byte order mark).

requirements.original: In case of "UTF-16" and "UTF-32" big-endian ordering shall be used (as described in clauses 10.4 and 10.7 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2]).
requirements.canonical: When `string_serialization` of `encvalue_unichar` is "UTF-16" or "UTF-32", big-endian ordering SHALL be used.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.3 -- In case of "UTF-16" and "UTF-32" big-endian ordering shall be used (as described in clauses 10.4 and 10.7 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2]).

requirements.original: function encvalue_unichar(in template(value) any inpar, in charstring enc in universal charstring encoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return universal charstring { return oct2unichar(bit2oct(encvalue(inpar, encoding_info, dynamic_encoding)), enc); }
requirements.canonical: A call encvalue_unichar(inpar, string_serialization, encoding_info, dynamic_encoding) IS equivalent to oct2unichar(bit2oct(encvalue(inpar, encoding_info, dynamic_encoding)), string_serialization).

requirements.original: The encvalue_unichar function first invokes the encvalue function in order to encode the value passed in the inpar parameter to a bitstring.
requirements.canonical: The `encvalue_unichar` function IS executed by first invoking `encvalue` to encode the value passed in `inpar` to a bitstring.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.3 -- The encvalue_unichar function first invokes the encvalue function in order to encode the value passed in the inpar parameter to a bitstring.

requirements.original: The bitstring is then converted to an octetstring by the bit2oct function and subsequently to a universal charstring using the oct2unichar function.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.3 -- The universal charstring value is then returned as the result of the encvalue_unichar function.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.3 -- In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are: Encoding fails due to a runtime system problem (i.e. no encoding function exists for the actual type of inpar).

requirements.original: function decvalue_unichar (inout universal charstring encoded_value, out any decoded_value, in charstring string_encoding := "UTF-8"", in universal charstring decoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return integer { var bitstring v_str = oct2bit(unichar2oct(encoded_value, string_encoding)); var integer v_result := decvalue(v_str, decoded_value, decoding_info, dynamic_encoding); if (v_result == 0) { // success encoded_value := oct2unichar(bit2oct(v_str), string_encoding); } return v_result; }
requirements.canonical: A call of `decvalue_unichar` IS equivalent to converting `encoded_value` with oct2bit(unichar2oct(encoded_value, string_serialization)), calling `decvalue` on the result with `decoded_value`, `decoding_info` and `dynamic_encoding`, and returning the `decvalue` result.

ambiguity.issue: The explanatory function and its description name the parameter `string_encoding` (with a stray quote in the default "UTF-8""), while the signature in C.5.4-s001 names it `string_serialization`.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.4 -- function decvalue_unichar (inout universal charstring encoded_value, out any decoded_value, in charstring string_encoding := "UTF-8"", in universal charstring decoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return integer { var bitstring v_str = oct2bit(unichar2oct(encoded_value, string_encoding)); var integer v_result := decvalue(v_str, decoded_value, decoding_info, dynamic_encoding); if (v_result == 0) { // success encoded_value := oct2unichar(bit2oct(v_str), string_encoding); } return v_result; }

requirements.original: The decvalue_unichar function first converts the universal charstring value passed in the encoded_value parameter into an octetstring using the unichar2oct function.
requirements.canonical: The `decvalue_unichar` function IS executed by first converting the universal charstring passed in `encoded_value` into an octetstring using `unichar2oct`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.4 -- The decvalue_unichar function first converts the universal charstring value passed in the encoded_value parameter into an octetstring using the unichar2oct function.

requirements.original: The string_encoding parameter controls how the characters are converted into octets (in fact how the bitstring sent to the codec contains the characters).
requirements.canonical: The `string_serialization` parameter of `decvalue_unichar` IS the control of how the characters are converted into octets (i.e. how the bitstring sent to the codec contains the characters).

ambiguity.issue: The explanatory function and its description name the parameter `string_encoding` (with a stray quote in the default "UTF-8""), while the signature in C.5.4-s001 names it `string_serialization`.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.4 -- The string_encoding parameter controls how the characters are converted into octets (in fact how the bitstring sent to the codec contains the characters).

requirements.original: The octetstring is subsequently converted into a bitstring by the oct2bit function.
requirements.canonical: The octetstring produced inside `decvalue_unichar` IS converted into a bitstring by `oct2bit`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.4 -- The octetstring is subsequently converted into a bitstring by the oct2bit function.

requirements.original: This bitstring is then passed as a parameter to the standard decvalue function that performs the actual decoding.
requirements.canonical: The bitstring produced inside `decvalue_unichar` IS passed to the standard `decvalue` function, which performs the actual decoding.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.4 -- This bitstring is then passed as a parameter to the standard decvalue function that performs the actual decoding.

requirements.original: In case of successful decoding, the undecoded part of the message is automatically converted from bitstring to octetstring by the bit2oct function and then to universal charstring using the oct2unichar function.
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue_unichar` is successful, the undecoded part of the message IS converted from bitstring to octetstring by `bit2oct` and then to universal charstring by `oct2unichar`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.4 -- In case of successful decoding, the undecoded part of the message is automatically converted from bitstring to octetstring by the bit2oct function and then to universal charstring using the oct2unichar function.

requirements.original: This universal charstring is then assigned to the encoded_value parameter.
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue_unichar` is successful, the universal charstring obtained from the undecoded part IS assigned to the `encoded_value` parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.4 -- This universal charstring is then assigned to the encoded_value parameter.

requirements.original: The result of decoding is then returned to the TE, finishing the decvalue_unichar call.
requirements.canonical: The result of the inner `decvalue` call IS returned to the caller as the result of `decvalue_unichar`.

ambiguity.issue: 'TE' (TTCN-3 Executable, a TRI/TCI concept) is not defined in the core language; the result is returned to the calling behaviour.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.4 -- The result of decoding is then returned to the TE, finishing the decvalue_unichar call.
